subject: DPA clarifications and data handling follow-up (controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@catalystfinancial.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:02:00-05:00
Subject: DPA clarifications — Catalyst Financial / Redwood

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick follow-up from our security and procurement teams — they asked for a few clarifications on the DPA and overall data handling before we can complete the legal review: 

- Controller/Processor: We need a short statement confirming Redwood's role (Controller vs Processor) for the services we discussed.
- Subprocessors: Can you provide the current subprocessors list and confirm whether Redwood will notify customers prior to adding new subprocessors (and what the notice period is)?
- Breach notice: What is Redwood's SLA for notifying customers about data breaches (initial notification timeframe and follow-up cadence)?
- Data residency: Can Redwood guarantee that customer production data can be kept within US regions? Are there Dedicated/Private options that affect residency?
- Data retention & PII: What are the default retention windows for logs, KV/prefix caches, and any PII extracted for prompt routing or troubleshooting? Is there an option to shorten/disable retention?
- Logging controls & access: What access controls and audit logs are available for customer data access by Redwood employees or subprocessors?

We've attached the procurement questionnaire to give context. Can you send the DPA with any clarifying language and subprocessors list? If possible, we'd like to get confirmation by end of week so we can schedule a procurement review next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Security Operations
Catalyst Financial

Attachment: Catalyst_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@catalystfinancial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T18:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — Catalyst Financial / Redwood

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear list — good questions. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap/answers:
- Roles: Redwood will be Processor and Catalyst Financial will be Controller for customer data processed via the Redwood inference API. We'll include explicit language in the DPA to that effect.
- Subprocessors: I'm attaching the current subprocessors list (managed infra, observability, payments). Redwood provides notice before adding new subprocessors; our standard notice period is 30 days, except in emergency scenarios where we'll notify as soon as practicable.
- Breach notice: Redwood's standard is to provide initial notification within 48 hours of confirming a security incident that affects customer data, with follow-ups as we have more information. We'll include this in the DPA breach notice clause.
- Data residency: Production customer data can be routed to specific regions for Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted API customers we offer region selection (US/EU) for newer accounts; we can put explicit residency commitments in a contract for Dedicated/Private.
- Retention & PII: Default logging retention is 90 days for platform logs and 30 days for request/response debug logs; KV cache and prefix caches are not persisted beyond the inference session unless configured/opted-in by the customer. We can add a contractual option to reduce retention windows or disable debug logging.
- Access & audit logs: We maintain role-based access controls, audited access logs, and customer-facing audit reports on request (SOC2 + per-route access logs available as part of enterprise package).

Next steps:
1) I'm attaching Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and Redwood_Subprocessors_List_20261119.csv.
2) Can you confirm which residency option you need (Hosted US, Dedicated US, Private on-prem)?
3) If it helps, I can loop in our legal (Dev Patel) and our solutions lead (Marissa) for a short call to walk through the DPA redline — suggest Tue 2026-11-24 morning ET.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (application/pdf), Redwood_Subprocessors_List_20261119.csv (text/csv)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@catalystfinancial.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — Catalyst Financial / Redwood

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our legal and security reviewers after looking at the attachments: 

- Subprocessor notification: 30 days is fine for normal additions. For EU-residency data we may require an opt-out right for specific subprocessors; is that something Redwood supports contractually for Dedicated/Private?
- Breach notice: 48 hours for initial notification is acceptable. Please confirm the escalation path and whether Redwood will provide a root-cause summary within 14 days where feasible.
- Retention: We need the option for a 30-day max retention for request/response logs and the ability to opt out of debug-level logging. Please confirm the operational impact and whether that requires Dedicated/Private.
- Audit logs: Can Redwood provide per-request access logs for admin access (who, when, reason) for a 12-month window as part of the enterprise package?

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to complete the legal review by 2026-11-27. A short call with your legal team next week would be ideal.

Best,
Aisha

Attachment: Catalyst_Procurement_Notes_20261119.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@catalystfinancial.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications — Catalyst Financial / Redwood

Ben / Marissa / Aisha —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick legal/ops callouts and proposed language we can commit to: 

1) Roles: Confirmed — Redwood Inference acts as Data Processor; Catalyst Financial is Data Controller. We will add an explicit recitation to Section 1 of the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: We've attached the current subprocessors list. Redwood will provide 30 days' notice prior to adding a new subprocessor; for emergency/security-critical additions we'll notify as soon as practicable and provide mitigation measures. For EU-residency customers on Dedicated/Private we can include contractual restrictions or an opt-out right for specific subprocessors — this is achievable but will need to be scoped per-account.

3) Breach notice: Redwood will provide initial notification within 48 hours of confirming an incident affecting customer data, followed by periodic updates. We will aim to provide a root-cause summary within 14 days if scope permits; otherwise we'll provide an interim update and a remediation plan.

4) Retention & PII: Default retention windows are as Ben described. We can contractually set a 30-day retention maximum for request/response logs and disable debug logging on a per-customer basis. For applications that require persistent KV caches for performance, we'll note this in the contract and document operational trade-offs. Dedicated/Private deployments make it easier to guarantee residency and stricter retention.

5) Audit logs & access: We can provide per-request access logs (who accessed, when, reason code) and retain those for 12 months as part of our enterprise observability add-on. This will be included as an enterprise option in the contract.

Next steps:
- I'll prepare a redline to Redwood_DPA_v3 with the language above and flag the residency/subprocessor opt-out as an account-level appendix.
- Suggest a 30-minute call Tue 2026-11-24 11:00 AM ET with Catalyst legal/security to walk through the redline. Ben — can you confirm availability and lock the invite?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.example.com
